events.text: I'll start by establishing a short list of specifications based on reasoning that doesn't depend on the data itself — these should reflect general, time-tested principles about return-predictive features (momentum, reversal, carry-type signals, combined with their natural sign conventions).

supports.rationale: Single feature momentum/trend proxy, long side bet that feature 1 captures a persistent directional signal
Combining two independent signals equal-weight to diversify idiosyncratic noise while preserving a common directional tilt
Three-feature equal-weight combo to average out noise further, classic ensemble diversification logic
Spread between two related features capturing relative-value/reversal dynamics, a common market-neutral construction
Contrarian/reversal bet on feature 1 in case the underlying signal is mean-reverting rather than trending

events.text: Now let me evaluate these short-listed specifications and explore the feature space systematically.
These are all weak/negative. Let me do a broader scan across single features to find which ones have genuine signal (in either direction), then build combinations from the best performers.

Interesting — feature 16 is strongly negative (-2.145), meaning its negation (+2.145 implied) could be a strong signal! And feature 11 at +0.106 is mildly positive. Let me flip feature 16's sign and continue scanning the rest of the features.

Good, features are indexed 0..39. I found strong negative Sharpes on features 16 (-2.703), 24 (-2.293), 37 (-1.364), 28 (-1.125). Flipping signs on these gives strong positive candidates. Let me check feature 0 (since indexing starts at 0, I haven't tested it) and verify the flipped signs.

Very interesting — this is a strong clue. Flipping the sign on feature 24 made it *more* negative (-2.293 → -3.037), not positive! That's unusual and tells me the relationship isn't simply "negate it" — this is suspicious of a non-stationary/non-linear effect, possibly driven by a few extreme days or the turnover-cost structure. Let me investigate feature 24 alone more carefully, and check if this is a turnover-cost artifact (i.e., the "signal" sign flip changes turnover in a nonlinear way due to costs).

This confirms something important: for feature 24, both signs give strongly negative Sharpe (-2.293 and -3.037). This can't happen for a simple linear long-short signal P&L unless there's something special — likely this "feature" has very high turnover (noisy/anti-persistent) so cost dominates regardless of sign, swamping any raw directional edge. That makes sense: evaluate nets out costs, and a feature that flips sign every day creates huge turnover costs that overwhelm the signal in both directions.

This tells me these high-magnitude-negative single features (16, 24, 28, 37) are likely **high turnover / noisy** features — bad building blocks regardless of sign. The better candidates are ones with modest Sharpe already (9 at +0.106 flipping to -0.106... wait let me recheck) — actually feature 9 was +0.106 earlier (long), the best single positive I found. Let me refocus on moderate, stable signals and try combinations among the mild performers.

Note: feature 9 at long sign gave -0.351 now (I think I mislabeled earlier — let me recheck, earlier "feature 9" long gave -0.351 both times consistently, and feature 11 gave +0.106). I confused feature 9 with 11. Let me redo carefully with feature 11, and also check 8, 10 (neighbors), and build around the genuinely best: feature 11 (+0.106), feature 22 (+0.058), feature 33 (+0.010), feature 29(-0.001 orig long, better flipped? let's check), feature 6 (-0.010 close to zero).

Progress — feature combo [11,12] short, and [11,12,22] with signs [1,-1,1] both give ~0.22. Let's explore around this neighborhood more: feature 12 alone (long gave -0.005, so short gives +0.005... small). The combination effect is better than individual parts, suggesting real diversification benefit. Let me refine further.

Feature 12 alone (short) gives 0.262, actually better than any 2-3 combo I've tried with it! Let me explore single feature 12 short more, and try pairing it with other candidates to see if I can beat 0.262.
[12,22] with signs [-1,1] gives 0.289, best so far. Let's refine around this pair with a third feature, and double check consistency.

The pair [12,22] with signs [-1,1] at 0.289 remains the best, and adding a third feature doesn't clearly improve it (0.288 with feature 6 is basically the same, within noise). This is a reasonable, fairly robust-looking signal. Let me do a bit more exploration of other unexplored feature pairs to make sure I'm not missing something stronger, then settle.

Several pairs with feature 12 (short) cluster around 0.24-0.29: [12,22]=0.289, [12,3]=0.280, [12,19]=0.281, [12,6]=0.244. This consistency suggests feature 12 (shorted) is the main driver and these other features are fairly interchangeable/correlated co-movers adding a little diversification. Let me try combining three of these together and also check if [12,3,22] type combos help, while being wary of overfitting to noise.

[12,3,22] with signs [-1,-1,1] gives 0.314, the best so far. This cluster (12, 3, 19, 22) all seem correlated and robustly point the same direction regardless of exact combo (0.28-0.31 range), which is a good sign of genuine (not overfit) signal rather than a lucky single combination. Let me do a final check of a couple more variations near this best candidate before settling.

events.text:
Confirmed: max 3 features is enforced. My best candidate remains **[12, 3, 22] with signs [-1, -1, 1]** at in-sample Sharpe 0.314. 

Individual components: feature 3 short (0.279), feature 12 short (0.262), feature 22 long (0.058) — each contributes positively, and the combination (0.314) exceeds any individual, consistent with real diversification rather than a fluke. This is a modest but fairly stable signal across neighboring specifications (0.28-0.31 range), which gives me reasonable confidence it's not purely overfit noise.

Given:
- In-sample Sharpe: 0.314
- Typical in-sample/out-of-sample degradation for a signal found via moderate search over 40 features (not a massive grid search, but with some feature mining involved)
- The robustness across similar nearby specs (reduces variance of my estimate of the "true" effect)

I'll set a conservative predicted OOS Sharpe below the in-sample value to account for selection effects, with a fairly wide uncertainty band.

I submitted my specification:

**Specification:** Equal-weight combination of feature 12 (short), feature 3 (short), feature 22 (long)
**In-sample Sharpe:** 0.314
**Predicted OOS Sharpe:** mean = 0.15, sd = 0.20

**Reasoning summary:**
1. I first tried theory-driven shortlist specs (momentum/reversal combos on arbitrary early features) — all were negative in-sample, showing my priors without data weren't useful here.
2. I then scanned all 40 features individually (long) to map the raw signal landscape. A few features showed large negative Sharpes in both long AND short directions (e.g., features 16, 24, 28, 37) — this is a signature of high-turnover/noisy features where transaction costs dominate regardless of sign, so I excluded them as poor building blocks.
3. I identified a cluster of mild, consistent performers (features 3, 12, 19, 22) that each showed modest positive Sharpe in a particular direction, and whose pairwise/triple combinations consistently landed in the 0.25–0.31 range — a sign of genuine, non-fluky signal rather than a lucky single draw.
4. The best 3-feature combination found was **{12: short, 3: short, 22: long}** at in-sample Sharpe 0.314, which beat every individual component, indicating real diversification benefit.
5. Because this was found via a search over many specifications (inflating the in-sample estimate relative to true OOS performance), I discounted my OOS mean estimate substantially (0.314 → 0.15) and assigned a wide standard deviation (0.20) to reflect genuine uncertainty about how much of the in-sample edge will persist out-of-sample.
